reference: Runnable expectations are Bash's documented type/help metadata contract and the swapoff builtin synopsis/documentation in loadables/swapoff.c and docs/sol-swapoff.md. There are no operation parity cases: invoking swapoff is expressly out of scope, and a denied syscall would not establish operational parity.
coverage: Bash identifies swapoff as a builtin with an empty candidate PATH.
Bash help exposes the builtin synopsis, short description, and documented behavior.
Deferred operation scopes identify the independent mock or disposable-VM requirements for named operands, -a table handling, and real kernel removal.
exclusions: No runnable case invokes the swapoff builtin or GNU util-linux swapoff; kernel swap changes are prohibited for this task.
The deferred operation cases are not passes and establish no swapoff syscall, /proc/swaps parsing, privilege, or kernel behavior.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves the statically loaded swapoff command as a builtin while candidate PATH is empty.
Verify Bash's documented -s mode prints the builtin usage synopsis supplied by the swapoff metadata.
Verify Bash help reports the documented short description for swapoff.
Check the built-in help includes path resolution, reverse -a table handling, combined operands, and the privilege contract without calling swapoff.
cases.script:
doc=$(help swapoff)
[[ $doc == *"Each spec is resolved before swapoff(2)."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"An existing path is canonicalized."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"-a reads /proc/swaps backwards, keeps duplicates, then walks fstab swap entries."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"A parse error is reported and the rest of the table is still attempted."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"-a may be combined with specs; the specs are disabled first."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"Requires root."* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented help fields present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise resolved named operands, -- for a leading dash, repeated explicit operands, and continuation/status behavior when a request fails.
Exercise -a/--all against controlled /proc/swaps data, including header handling, octal path decoding, duplicate rows kept in reverse order, malformed rows, and valid-row continuation.
Establish end-to-end behavior when the kernel actually disables swap and removes that area from the active table.
